title: Preparing others
tomorrow: who pays for the lights at church, and why should anyone care?

lines: A CHARIOT ON A DESERT ROAD.
HOW CAN I, UNLESS SOMEONE SHOWS ME?
cards: A kid asks the big question at the worst moment: in the car, mid-bite, no warning. Is it really Jesus? Where do people go when they die?
And you freeze. Acts has a scene on a desert road. An official from Ethiopia is riding home in his chariot, reading the prophet Isaiah aloud, and not getting it.
Philip runs up alongside and asks: do you understand what you're reading? The man answers, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "And how can I, unless some man shew me?"

teach.b: So Philip climbs up and sits beside him. He doesn't lecture from the roadside.

He starts from the very passage the man is stuck on, and from there tells him about Jesus. Then they pass some water, and the official asks what's to stop him being baptized. Philip baptizes him there.
Notice the shape: sit beside, start where they are, walk them in. One to tell a friend: this Philip is one of the seven chosen to serve tables, back in Acts 6.

That's what the Church asks of catechists, the people who prepare others for the sacraments. Pope Francis made catechist an instituted ministry and called it a vocation of service. You don't need every answer to do it.
Children preparing for First Communion learn what the Church believes, that Christ is truly present in the Eucharist, which the Catechism calls the source and summit of the Christian life.
And it's honest to tell a curious kid: that's a great question, let's find out together. Godparents and sponsors do the same work.
They walk beside someone before the big day, and after it.

how: Parish catechists prepare children for First Communion and Confirmation, and adults joining the Church walk with sponsors through the Order of Christian Initiation of Adults.

games.q: you're Philip. you've run up beside the chariot, and the man says he can't understand without someone to guide him. what next?
o: climb up, sit beside him, and start from his passage.
give him a reading list and wish him a safe trip.
tell him to come back to Jerusalem for proper classes.
games.why: Philip sat with him and began from that very scripture. by the time they reached water, the man asked to be baptized.

practice: Bring to mind someone preparing for a step right now: a child before First Communion, a friend before Confirmation, an adult joining the Church, or anyone facing something big.
Send them a short message that asks for nothing back, something like thinking of you, glad you're doing this. If you pray, you can pray for them as it sends.

wordCard.voice: Preparing others. Walking beside someone toward a sacrament, starting where they are, without needing every answer. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: will guide. the official's word in Acts 8:31: how can I, unless someone guides me?

carryVoice: Hold onto this: walk them in, the way Philip climbed up and sat beside the man first. Rest well.
